title: 07 Exponents and radicals: Visual Guide
outline: Title: 07 Exponents and radicals: Visual Guide

1. Counting The Factors | the binomial and powers-of-i habits you already have, beside the three exponent properties, with m, n and a numeric base dragged live so each rule is expanded into factors and checked against the wrong rule | an integer exponent is a count of repeated factors, so multiplying adds the counts, nesting multiplies them and dividing subtracts them top minus bottom

2. Zero And Negative Powers | a ladder of b^4 down to b^-4 where every rung divides by the base, with the quotient-rule derivation rewritten as the exponent crosses zero and the x/2, 2/x and -x^2 misreadings computed alongside | x^0 = 1 and x^-n = 1/x^n are forced by the quotient rule rather than decreed, and a negative exponent inverts the value without ever making it negative

3. Pull Out Squares | a draggable radicand from 2 to 144 with every perfect square that divides it lit up, the largest one factored out step by step, and the answer squared back to the original | simplifying a square root means extracting the largest perfect square, because only a squared factor can leave the radical, and a partial extraction is correct but unfinished

4. When Radicals Combine | two rules side by side - adding a√p + c√q with the add-the-radicands and multiply-the-coefficients errors computed, and splitting √(ab) with both radicands draggable through zero | like radicals add as like terms with the radicand untouched, while √(ab) = √a·√b is guaranteed only for nonnegative radicands and genuinely fails when both are negative

5. Growth Or Decay | the graph of y = b^x with the base dragged across 1, a table of values and the constant ratio per step, plus an optional overlay of y = x^3 and y = 3x + 1 | b > 1 rises ever more steeply and 0 < b < 1 decays toward the y = 0 asymptote, every such curve passes through (0, 1), and only a variable in the exponent is exponential at all
